19-player-publish/shared-rules/pulp-comb.title: Pulp Combat Damage
19-player-publish/shared-rules/pulp-comb.description: Category: combat Natural Healing – +2 HP per day (Quick Healer talent bumps this to +3 HP/day). First Aid / Medicine Boost – Successful rolls heal +1D4 HP (Extreme success = 4 HP). No Major‑Wound Penalty – Heroes do not suffer the usual major‑wound effects. Death Thresholds Instant death: Single attack ≥ maximum HP. Dying: Single attack ≥ ½ maximum HP and reduces HP to 0. Unconscious: HP drops to 0 (but not ≥ ½ max). Half‑HP Shock: If a single blow cuts HP by ≥ ½ max and leaves the hero above 0, they must make a CON roll to stay conscious. Dying State – Mark current HP as “D” (dying). CON Rolls – Made at the end of each round; any failure = immediate death. Stabilizing First Aid (success) → removes “D”, restores 1D4 HP (Extreme = 4 HP). Extreme Cases (e.g., being ripped apart) may render First Aid impossible – death is inevitable. Follow‑up Medicine – After stabilization, a successful Medicine roll adds another 1D4 HP (Extreme = 4 HP). Base Rate – +2 HP/day (or +3 HP/day with Quick Healer). Medical Assistance – Each successful daily Medicine roll adds 1 HP to that day’s natural healing (total +3 HP). Modifiers – Hospital care may grant a bonus die; unsanitary conditions may impose a penalty die. Failed Medicine – May reduce healing (e.g., lose 1 HP or, on a pushed roll, lose 1D3 HP). Near‑Death Trauma – Typically triggers a Sanity roll (0 or 1 SAN loss depending on outcome). Role‑Playing Hook – Encourage players to describe lingering injuries (broken limbs, missing fingers, etc.) for dramatic effect, but remember pulp heroes can often “brush it off.” Spending Luck – A dying hero may expend all remaining Luck points (minimum 30 LP required) to cheat death. Result of Luck Spend Luck drops to 0. Hero immediately regains 1D6 + 1 HP. Injuries remain; further healing still required. No further CON rolls needed for that death episode. Narrative Requirement – Player must describe how the hero miraculously survives. Max HP = 22, current = 8. Trap deals 18 damage → HP = ‑10 → Dying (≥ ½ max, reduced to 0). First Aid succeeds → “D” removed, 1D4 HP restored (e.g., 3 HP). Medicine roll succeeds → additional 1D4 HP (e.g., 4 HP). Natural healing resumes (+2 HP/day, possibly +1 HP from daily Medicine). Max HP = 34, current = 17. Star‑spawn claw deals 19 damage → HP = ‑2 → Dying (≥ ½ max, reduced to 0). Luck spend (≥ 30 LP) → Luck → 0, regain 1D6 + 1 HP (e.g., 5 HP). CON roll at end of round succeeds → remains conscious. Allies apply First Aid (success) → +1D4 HP (e.g., 3 HP). Daily Medicine rolls add extra HP each day (+1 HP per successful roll). Facing instant death from Cthulhu’s foot, Maximillian spends all 36 Luck (≥ 30). Describes a cinematic survival (e.g., diving behind a shattered column, a gust of wind lifting him). Luck drops to 0, he regains 1D6 + 1 HP, avoids death, and continues the chase. Back to Shared Rules

19-player-publish/shared-rules/pulp-luck.title: Pulp Luck Spending
19-player-publish/shared-rules/pulp-luck.description: Category: pulpPulp Cthulhu – Luck‑Spend Options (Quick‑Reference Table) Luck Cost is expressed in the amount of Luck points that must be spent from the character’s (or NPC’s) Luck pool. When a rule says “all Luck points,” the entire remaining pool is consumed. Identify the situation (e.g., you just failed a Sanity roll, or you’re about to die). Find the matching row to see what the Luck spend accomplishes. Check the cost and verify you have enough Luck points. Declare the spend to the Keeper; apply the effect immediately. Feel free to adapt or house‑rule any of these options to suit the tone of your campaign!Back to Shared Rules

info_allowGlobalGraph.description: Allow the user to view the global graph of all nodes.

info_allowExpand.description: Allow the user to pop-out the graph view to take up the whole screen

info_attractionForce.description: How much should linked nodes attract each other? This will make the graph appear more clustered.

info_linkLength.description: How long should the links between nodes be? The shorter the links the more connected nodes will cluster together.

info_repulsionForce.description: How much should nodes repel each other? This will make disconnected parts more spread out.

info_centralForce.description: How much should nodes be attracted to the center? This will make the graph appear more dense and circular.

info_edgePruning.description: Edges with a length above this threshold will not be rendered, however they will still contribute to the simulation. This can help large tangled graphs look more organised. Hovering over a node will still display these links.

info_minNodeRadius.description: How small should the smallest nodes be? The smaller a node is the less it will attract other nodes.

info_maxNodeRadius.description: How large should the largest nodes be? Nodes are sized by how many links they have. The larger a node is the more it will attract other nodes. This can be used to create a good grouping around the most important nodes.
